title: Taxpayer Experience Improvement Act
summary: This bill requires the IRS to publish real-time data on its public website about phone wait times, call volumes, and processing backlogs for every public phone line it operates, and to make that data available through a public API so third-party apps can display it. It also requires the IRS to give taxpayers online or mobile access to their own tax returns, notices, and refund status including an estimated delivery date.
brief: Requires the IRS to publish live phone wait times and backlog data, and give taxpayers digital access to their own returns and refund status.

top_lines.headline: Real-Time IRS Dashboard
subs: IRS must publish live caller counts, wait times, and callback availability per phone line on its public website
Public API required so any person or app can access the live call data

top_lines.headline: Digital Tax Record Access
subs: Taxpayers can view all returns, notices, and IRS letters via website or mobile app
IRS must provide estimated refund receipt date

top_lines.headline: Monthly Accountability Metrics
subs: IRS must publish monthly averages for call length, hold time, disconnection rate, and percent of callers who got help
Sense of Congress: callback offered within 5 minutes on any unanswered call by 2028

likelihoodReason: Only 1 cosponsor despite bipartisan sponsorship (Schweikert R-AZ and Beyer D-VA). IRS modernization bills often pass the House but stall in the Senate amid disagreements over IRS funding and IT capacity. The real-time dashboard and public API requirements may face resistance from the Treasury Department over implementation feasibility.

items.main: Names the Act the “Taxpayer Experience Improvement Act”, defines “Secretary” as the Secretary of the Treasury or delegate, and lists the Act's table of contents.
items.detail: Short-title/definitions/table-of-contents section — citation name, the “Secretary” reference, and a navigational contents list; no substantive effect.

items.main: Requires the IRS to publish in real time on its public website call volume, wait time, and callback availability for each applicable phone number extension.
items.detail: For each phone line, the IRS must display the number of callers connected to representatives, connected to automated systems, and waiting; the longest current wait time; and whether callback service is available. A public API must be provided for automated access to the data. The IRS must also detect and screen automated calls, and publish processing delay information weekly when significant backlogs occur.

items.main: Requires monthly summary statistics for each phone line, including caller satisfaction data.
items.detail: Monthly metrics must include average and median call lengths and hold times; the percent of calls disconnected or directed to automation; the number of callers transferred; and the number and percent of callers who indicated they received the help they were seeking. The last metric requires the IRS to actively collect caller satisfaction data before calls end.

sections.label: Section 3 — Expansion of Electronic Access to Information About Returns and Refunds

items.main: Requires the Secretary, via website and mobile application, to give taxpayers individualized, up-to-date status on their returns and amended returns — receipt, completed processing (with refund date and estimated receipt date), or suspension with the reason and any requested information.
items.detail: Deadline: not later than January 1 of the first calendar year beginning more than 12 months after enactment. For electronic refunds, must show the partial/full account number plus the institution's name and routing number; for paper checks, the mailing address.

items.main: Expresses the sense of Congress that taxpayers should be able to request a callback, and that by calendar year 2028 the IRS should offer a callback for any call to an applicable phone number extension not answered within 5 minutes.
items.detail: Sense-of-Congress provision (non-binding); applies to any taxpayer, including those residing outside the United States.

items.main: Requires the Secretary to make available a website or mobile application letting any taxpayer view returns, documents, notices and letters from the prior 6-year period, respond to IRS notices online, and authorize representatives, preparers, or qualified reporting agents to access them.
items.detail: Deadline: not later than January 1 of the first calendar year beginning more than 18 months after enactment. Consistent with section 6103 of the Internal Revenue Code. Also requires a program to investigate unauthorized access by designated persons (with annual public reporting) and taxpayer/tax-professional focus groups before launch.

underreported.summary: The monthly statistics requirement includes the number and percent of callers who indicated they received the answers or service they were seeking — a customer satisfaction data point embedded in a call-volume reporting requirement.
underreported.why_unreported: Collecting this metric requires the IRS to actively ask callers before they hang up whether their issue was resolved, effectively mandating a caller survey process. This is a new operational requirement distinct from passively logging call volume and wait times, not apparent from the bill's IRS dashboard framing.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Schweikert
featured_quotes.text: I ask the chairman whether it is tireless or annoying. It is one or the other. Look, I have an absolute fixation, and I have got to thank my Democratic colleague and a number of the team here for tolerating my fixation on the fact that one of the ways you work within the IRS budget to make things more efficient is the adoption of technology. Imagine a world--because it is the one we live in--where some of the number one calls we get to my district office are IRS questions: Where is my refund? Do I owe money?

gaps: The bill requires real-time call data but does not specify a minimum uptime requirement for the dashboard or what disclosures are required if the live data is unavailable.
The digital access requirement does not specify an implementation timeline for the mobile application option, nor minimum device or accessibility standards for the application.

added: Requirement for real-time IRS public dashboard with per-phone-line call volume, wait times, and callback availability, plus public API access
Monthly IRS reporting requirement including caller satisfaction metrics, disconnection rates, and hold times per phone extension
Requirement for IRS to provide taxpayers with online or mobile access to returns, notices, refund status, and estimated refund date
Requirement for IRS to use technology to detect and screen automated calls
